A_target.statement:
Let $G$ be a finite [[Definition:Directed Graph|directed graph]] and $u \sim v$ {{iff}} each is reachable from the other.
Then $\sim$ is an equivalence relation, whose classes are the [[Definition:Strongly Connected Component|strongly connected components]], and the condensation $G / \sim$ is a [[Definition:Directed Acyclic Graph|directed acyclic graph]].

B_source.statement:
Let $\preceq$ be a [[Definition:Preordering|preorder]] on a set $P$, and $x \approx y$ {{iff}} $x \preceq y$ and $y \preceq x$.
Then $\approx$ is an equivalence relation and $\preceq$ descends to a [[Definition:Partial Ordering|partial order]] on $P / \approx$.

object_map.reformulation: Quotient the reachability preorder by its symmetric part; the resulting partial order cannot contain a cycle.

validity_conditions: Reachability is reflexive and transitive, so it is a preorder.
Strongly connected components can be computed in linear time by Tarjan's algorithm, which then yields a topological order.
proof_plan: Reachability $\leadsto$ is reflexive and transitive, hence a preorder, and $\sim$ is its symmetric part, with classes the strongly connected components.
By the source result, $\leadsto$ descends to a partial order on the components.

Each edge of $G / \sim$ between distinct components lies in this order.
A directed cycle through distinct components would make them mutually reachable, hence equal by antisymmetry.

Hence $G / \sim$ is acyclic, and its components can be listed in a topological order.
{{qed}}
